name: Topping
_terms_TWO_HOSTS_TWO_SITUATIONS_not_merg: Measured 2026-11-25. tpdz.net, www.tpdz.net, topping.audio and www.topping.audio ALL 301 redirect to www.toppingaudio.com, which is the maker's current product host; dl.topping.audio is the manual host. On the product host the full 328-entry sitemap was pulled and every likely terms path returns 404; the only legal-ish page is /warranty-terms, read in full, whose single reservation - « *TOPPING company reserves the final interpretation and amendment for the above terms » - is about the warranty. Footer: « (c) 2026 TOPPING Technology co., LTD. All rights reserved. » On dl.topping.audio there is no terms page AND no copyright footer at all: its index is an unconfigured web-panel placeholder titled « 恭喜，站点创建成功！ », and /um/, /usermanual/ and /marketing/ refuse directory listings with 403. Two absences, not one, and neither is permission. robots.txt on the product host is one « User-agent: * » group, « Allow: / » with three /api/ disallows, no Content-Signal, no Claude group; the download host has no robots.txt. THE /api/ PATHS SERVE THE SITE'S SPEC DATA AND WERE NOT FETCHED, which is why the image-only spec tables could not be routed around.
_nine_text_manuals_out_of_eighty_seven_f: The complete manual catalogue was enumerated - seven pages of /supports?tab=manual cross-checked against the Chinese list, 62 entries resolving to 87 distinct files - and extracted in DEFAULT pdftotext mode. Only NINE carry a text layer, all recent and under /um/; everything under /usermanual/ and the older /um/ files are pure rasters with no embedded fonts, where pdftotext returns nothing but page breaks (dx9.pdf: 62 pages, 62 form-feeds, 0 characters). « Specifications » survives intact in all nine. Of the nine, FIVE contain a converter: DX1 II, DX5 II, DX9 Discrete, D900 and E50 II. Those five are the whole text route into this maker's range.
_NO_converter_part_number_in_any_text_To: All nine text manuals grepped for ES9, AK4, CS43, PCM17, « DAC chip » and « chipset »: zero matches. Converter part numbers exist only inside the product pages' spec IMAGES, so `chip` and `family` are absent on every Topping record written from a manual. The two older import-sourced records under this brand, for the DX7 Pro and the E30, do carry a family - from a different source, at import weight.
_everything_else_is_image_only_and_here_: No text route exists to the D10 Balanced, D10s, D30 Pro, D50s, D50 III, D70 Pro SABRE, D70 Pro OCTO, D90SE, D90LE, D90 III SABRE, D90 III Discrete, DM7, Centaurus, E30 II, E30 II Lite, E50, E70, E70 Velvet, EX5, DX1, DX3 Pro+, DX5, DX5 Lite, DX7 Pro+, DX9, EHA5, G5, M50 or U90 - image-only on both the product page and the manual. And the maker publishes NO manual at all for the original D10, D30, D50, D70, D90 and D90 MQA, DX3 Pro, DX7, DX7s, DX7 Pro or E30: there is no plain D10, D50, D70 or D90 page on the current site. The legacy host v2.toppingaudio.com, which might still hold them, is unreachable - TLS certificate name mismatch, not bypassed.
_Topping_has_no_dongle_DAC: /products-list/portable contains exactly three items: a Bluetooth receiver, the G5 portable DAC/amplifier whose manual is image-only, and an analogue headphone amplifier. The nearest things elsewhere in the catalogue are a cable, two USB isolators and the U90 USB interface - none is a dongle DAC. Nothing to harvest there.
